anti_claims_ruled_out: Our results describe a different fit from Epoch's (W2).
Robustness in W5 comes from metrics that cannot detect sensitivity, or from perturbations too small to matter (C1 anti-claim; W3 positive control).
Clean checks in W4 come from checks with no power (C2 anti-claim; W3 power runs).
A fixed one-dimensional model hides structure that moves the scores (exploratory, W6).
why_this_block_exists: One Bayesian workflow on Epoch's model (Gelman, Vehtari, McElreath et al. 2026, Bayesian Workflow), replacing four separate audits of a fixed model: prior predictive check (W1), fit and reproduction (W2), computational and check calibration by simulation from the fitted posterior (W3), posterior predictive and LOO-PIT checks (W4), prior sensitivity (W5) and model expansion with comparison (W6). The stages share the W2 fit, the W3 refits and one set of frozen check code, so each stage's output is the next stage's input.
dataset_split_task: Fit input: epoch_capabilities_index/processed_data_for_eci.csv inside the zip (57 benchmarks, 256 models, 2879 rows). W1: prior predictive simulation on its (model, benchmark) pattern. W2: Epoch's fit on the fit input (W2a) and on the output of prepare_benchmark_data(zip) (W2b, three different GPQA diamond scores: Claude Fable 5 0.957 vs 0.845; Claude Opus 5.5 0.959 vs 0.911; Claude Fable 5.2 0.986 vs 0.957), plus our reimplementation of the base model (equivalence check EQ, M12). W3: data simulated on the observed pattern (M4): G-null (199 replicates from the fitted posterior, also the SBC replicates) and five misfit generators with 20 replicates each; the real data refitted with the positive-control prior. W4: the real data and its 5 folds over the 217 models with 6 or more scores (M7). W5: the real data under the prior grid. W6: the real data under the candidate models F0-F6 (M14), with PSIS-LOO over all 2,879 rows or K-fold over the 2,704 eligible rows.
systems_compared: W2a: fit_bayesian_eci(processed_data_for_eci.csv) with defaults, seeds 12345, 22345, 32345, against the published eci_scores.csv, edi_scores.csv, eci_bootstraps.json
W2b: fit_bayesian_eci(prepare_benchmark_data(zip)), seed 12345 (data-provenance check, reported, not gated)
EQ: our reimplementation F0 against Epoch's fit, seeds 12345 and 22345
W3: the default ECI fit on each G-null and misfit replicate; the positive-control prior against the W2 fits

W5: the baseline P0, its second-seed copy P0b, P1-P10, the stress priors X1 and X2, and the exploratory reference prior PR; added post-freeze (R26), the exploratory normalised Jeffreys priors J1 and J2, each fitted once like PR

W6: F0 (base, Epoch's priors), F1 two-dimensional capability, F2 developer-by-benchmark offset, F3 upper asymptote below 1, F4 time drift, F5 per-model noise scale, F6 (base under PR), and at most one combined model F7
fixed_factors: observation pattern of the real data
default BayesianPriors except where a stage varies them
check implementations in runs/lib/ppc_checks.py, runs/lib/sbc.py, runs/lib/sens_metrics.py and runs/lib/compare.py as frozen
W5 sampler: 4 chains, target_accept 0.95, draws=4000 per chain, seed 12345
metrics: W1: share of prior-simulated scores at the clip bounds and in [0.1, 0.9], per dataset, for Epoch's priors and PR; the PR criterion (mean mid-range share >= 0.40, at least 95% of datasets >= 0.15, mean bound share <= 0.35). Added post-freeze (R26): the same quantities for the normalised Jeffreys priors J1 and J2, by direct simulation, descriptive only

W2: per model d_m = ECI_ours - ECI_published and d_m / W_m,published (seed 12345); Spearman over 256 models; interval-width ratio; max abs difference of edi and slope (reported); divergences, r_hat, bulk and tail ESS, BFMI, stage and attempts; seed-to-seed SD; W2b S1-S4 against W2a; EQ density difference, per-model difference, Spearman, width ratio and elpd_loo difference

W3: recovery coverage overall and by stratum; SBC normalised ranks of ECI and EDI, per-parameter chi-square tests and pooled 50% and 90% coverage by stratum (M13); null reference values of T1-T7 from the converged G-null replicates (target 199); power of each targeted check; S1-S4 of the positive-control prior per seed; non-converged counts

W4: Epoch's suite as shipped (W4a); T1-T7 unadjusted, max-T adjusted and raw p (W4b); held-out 90% coverage overall and per benchmark with a model-cluster bootstrap interval (W4c); relative ECI shift per model after removing the localised set F (W4d)

W5: S1 Spearman, S2 share shifting by more than a quarter of the interval width, S3 interval-width ratio, S4 top-10 set and adjacent-pair probabilities, per stratum; S5 psens of the hyperpriors (decisive) and of each hyperprior separately (reported); noise floor; P(model in top 10); raw-scale S2 and S3 and posterior mass beyond abs 49 (reported)

W6: PSIS-LOO elpd and SE of the difference to F0, Pareto-k shares, K-fold elpd where triggered, computational diagnostics and reduced-SBC coverage of each preferred expansion, the adequate set, and S1-S4 and interval-width change of ECI under each adequate model relative to F0
setup_details: Stage order and dependencies are in the stage table of experiment-plan.md and the stage hand-offs of execution-bridge.md; one wrapper, runs/w_run.py, runs a stage or all of them and stops at a failed gate. W1 simulates and sets nothing. W2 fits with evaluate=True, adds the summed hyperprior log density (group log_prior) and the per-draw ECI to each trace, and fits our F0 for EQ. W3 freezes the check code, runs the positive control first, then G-null, then the misfit generators; replicate seed = first 4 bytes of sha256('<generator>:<index>'); the SBC ranks and the T values come from the same refits. W4 reads the W2 trace and the W3 reference values. W5 runs the S5 screen on the W2 seed-12345 draws first, then P0 and P0b and the noise floor, then every grid entry including PR, then the targeted refits. W6 starts only after the C1 and C2 verdicts are recorded and their files digested in runs/freeze.json.
success_criterion: W2 (G0): seed 12345 abs(d_m) <= max(0.5, 0.07 x W_m,published) for every non-anchor model, Spearman >= 0.999, median width ratio in [0.95, 1.05] and at least 95% of the 254 ratios in [0.85, 1.15]; all three seeds zero divergences, r_hat <= 1.01, bulk ESS >= 400. W3 (G1): recovery coverage over all non-anchor models in [0.85, 0.95]; at least 150 converged null replicates; T2 power >= 0.8 on G-2D and T5 power >= 0.8 on G-offset (16 of 20); the positive-control prior fails at least one of S1-S4 in the frontier or all-models stratum on all three seeds. W4 (G3): C2 decision rule. W5 (G2): C1 decision rule. W1 has no gate. W6 (G7, exploratory): equivalence check EQ passed; an expansion is preferred only if its elpd difference to F0 exceeds 4 and 2.5 standard errors, and adopted only if its computational checks and reduced SBC pass.
minimum_effect_size: 0.5 ECI points, or 0.07 of the published width where larger (G0); power 0.8 at family-wise alpha 0.01 (G1); adjusted p < 0.01, coverage outside [0.85, 0.95], binomial p < 0.01 / 44 (G3); a quarter of a model's baseline interval width, 1.1 to 1.9 ECI points for the 20 frontier models (G2); elpd difference above 4 (G7).
failure_interpretation: W2: production settings or data differ from the public ones; find the difference or rebaseline openly. W3: poor recovery means the published intervals are miscalibrated even when the model is true; a check without power cannot support C2. W4: W4d measures how far a localised misfit moves the scores. W5: a sparse-only failure narrows C1, a frontier or all-models failure falsifies it. W6: an adopted expansion is a finding about model structure and is reported beside, never instead of, the verdicts on Epoch's model.
compute_budget: W1 about 5 minutes (no fits). W2 6 fits (4 Epoch, 2 of ours), about 30 minutes. W3 302 fits, about 10 hours (about 40 CPU-hours), restartable. W4 about 30 minutes. W5 up to 23 fits (14 grid, PR, up to 2 C1 follow-ups, up to 6 exploratory targeted refits), about 1 to 2 hours; the post-freeze exploratory fits of J1 and J2 (R26) are two more fits of PR's size, outside this count. W6 about 3 to 10 hours typical and up to about 24 hours in the worst case, plus up to 8 hours if the combination F7 is fitted (M14); exploratory and stoppable. Without W6 the plan is about 13.5 hours; with W6 about 17 to 24 hours typical (worst case about 46 hours). Under 2 GB RAM per fit; about 3.5 GB disk.
selection_rule: Grid, check list, statistics, strata, generators, thresholds and the candidate list F0-F7 are fixed before any refit (digests in runs/freeze.json). Planted effect sizes and the seed rule are fixed in M4; fold assignment from numpy default_rng(20261113) as in M7. W6 fits every listed candidate; none is dropped after its elpd is seen.
non_vacuity_check: The W2 comparison can fail; the positive-control prior must fail S1-S4 in W3 or G1 tightens S2 once; a check counts towards 'Adequate' only if its targeted generator gave power >= 0.8; T6 and T7 are 'power not assessed'; the W1 prior predictive check can fail for PR, which is then dropped; EQ can fail, which blocks W6.
complete_outcome_accounting: Every seed, replicate, fold, grid entry and candidate model is reported with its convergence status; non-converged replicates are counted and excluded from the null reference, SBC and power; unresolved grid entries are reported as unresolved; every W6 candidate is listed with its elpd, including the ones not preferred.
hidden_information_controls: Grid, metric code, check code, SBC code and thresholds frozen by digest before use; true simulation parameters written only to runs/W/W3/truth/, which ppc_checks.py never reads; held-out scores removed before sampling; the C1 and C2 verdict files are digested before any W6 elpd is computed.
independence_requirements: Self-review only; simulation and analysis by the same agent; no independence claimed.
independence_evidence: None claimed; confirmatory status of C1 and C2 rests on pre-registration, not independence.

anti_claims_ruled_out: Low coverage from crosswalk errors or from evaluation-setup variance (C3 anti-claim).
why_this_block_exists: Finds the EEE data that correspond to ECI's benchmarks and models and tests whether ECI's intervals predict them.
dataset_split_task: B4a crosswalk (M9): all 122,861 aggregate records of EEE manifest dd7efcff (129 collections, 2.2 GB) are downloaded and screened; every evaluation result is mapped, or not, to one of the 57 ECI benchmarks and to an Epoch model group. Named-benchmark collections expected to match include gpqa-diamond, gpqa_diamond, frontiermath, arc-agi, terminal-bench-2.0, cybench, apex-agents, gsm8k, hellaswag, piqa and big_bench_hard; multi-benchmark collections to screen result by result include artificial-analysis-llms, vals-ai, paperswithcode, hfopenllm_v2, llm-stats, openeval, benchpress, wild and helm_*. Scores are normalised with Epoch's random_baseline and score_ceiling. B4b: ECI predictive distribution for each matched pair (M8).
systems_compared: ECI predictive distribution (W2 seed-12345 fit; the C3 verdict is defined on this model)
exploratory add-on: the same coverage under each adequate expansion of W6, if any
EEE-vs-EEE agreement on the same model x benchmark (noise floor)
same-upstream pairs (for example ARC Prize, Terminal-Bench, Mercor APEX) as the crosswalk positive control
variable_factors: Epoch's own score for the pair in the fit or not
metrics: crosswalk counts by class and exclusion reason
audit errors among 50 random matched pairs, with Clopper-Pearson 95% upper bound
same-upstream median and 90th percentile absolute difference
90% coverage on independent pairs with a 90% model-cluster bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples)
coverage split by in-fit / not-in-fit and by benchmark
EEE-vs-EEE agreement rate
signed mean difference (EEE minus ECI predictive mean) per benchmark
sensitivity: coverage after removing independent pairs whose raw score equals Epoch's to 3 decimals; coverage excluding pairs with Pareto k > 0.7
exploratory: coverage on the same pairs under each adequate W6 expansion, reported beside the verdict
setup_details: Stage a (no ECI predictions loaded): download objects, verify sha256 against the manifest, build runs/B4/collection_screen.csv, benchmark_map.csv, model_map.csv and source_class.csv by the rules in M9, classify every result, aggregate to pairs, draw the audit sample, audit, and freeze the maps (digests in runs/freeze.json). Stage b (only after the audit passes): join the W2 posterior, compute PIT, coverage, agreement and bias; if W6 has adequate expansions, repeat the coverage under each (exploratory). One wrapper runs both: runs/b4_run.py --stage a|b|all.
success_criterion: C3 decision rule with its preconditions: audit errors <= 2 of 50, same-upstream median absolute difference <= 0.02, at least 100 independent pairs over 20 model groups and 5 benchmarks, and coverage >= 0.80 with agreement not below 0.80.
failure_interpretation: More than 2 audit errors stop stage b until one round of fixes and a fresh audit sample. Low coverage with agreement >= 0.80 falsifies C3; agreement below 0.80 gives the verdict `harness-limited`.
compute_budget: Download and parse 122,861 JSON objects (2.2 GB); no new fits. 2 to 4 hours wall-clock, mostly I/O, plus the manual mapping and audit.
selection_rule: Inclusion, exclusion and source class are decided from metadata (benchmark version, split, metric, model identity, source organisation) before ECI predictions are computed for any pair.
non_vacuity_check: Same-upstream pairs give a case where the comparison must succeed; EEE-vs-EEE agreement gives the rate a perfect index could reach.
complete_outcome_accounting: Every EEE result is classified into exactly one class of the C3 loss contract; counts per class, collection and benchmark are reported; failed downloads are listed.
hidden_information_controls: Crosswalk built and audited without loading ECI predictions; stage b refuses to run unless the map digests match runs/freeze.json.
independence_requirements: EEE data are independent of Epoch only for pairs classed 'independent' by M9; the class is recorded per pair.
independence_evidence: source_metadata.source_organization_name, source_type and evaluator_relationship per EEE record, against the source column of Epoch's row.
